memoryAids.title: Explicit Instruction: I Do, We Do, You Do - With Data
memoryAids.content: Explain and model the strategy, guide many responses with feedback, then release independent practice when evidence shows readiness. Return to guidance when error patterns require it.

memoryAids.title: UDL: Goal, Barrier, Option
memoryAids.content: Clarify the learning goal, anticipate the barrier, and select purposeful options for engagement, representation, or action and expression that preserve the goal.
memoryAids.reviewNote: Retrieval cue only; verify current law and apply the underlying concept rather than memorizing the phrase alone.

memoryAids.title: ABC to Function

constructedResponseWorkshops.title: Separate Second-Language Needs from SLD While Honoring Evaluation Timelines
constructedResponseWorkshops.prompt: Analyze Sofia's Tier 2 reading CBM data, implementation logs, and multilingual history to recommend a legally compliant IDEA evaluation plan and immediate MTSS adjustments.
constructedResponseWorkshops.stimulus: Sofia (Grade 4, Spanish home language, 2.5 years in U.S. schools, WIDA 2.7) reads 46 words correct per minute on English CBM (benchmark 94; slope 0.6/week over 7 weeks). Logs show she missed 8 of 21 Tier 2 sessions for ESL pullout. In Spanish she reads Grade 3 texts at 92% accuracy and solves oral math word problems accurately. Her mother emailed a written IDEA evaluation request yesterday, but the MTSS lead wants to wait 12 more weeks.
taskParts: Evaluate why the English CBM score and flat Tier 2 slope cannot by themselves confirm a Specific Learning Disability without auditing dosage fidelity and language-acquisition factors.
Explain the IDEA Child Find and procedural response required after the mother's written evaluation request, including why MTSS cannot be used to delay or deny an initial evaluation.
Design a nondiscriminatory, multidisciplinary evaluation plan under 34 CFR 300.304 alongside immediate Tier 2 schedule and English language scaffold repairs.

planningFrame.label: Evidence
planningFrame.guidance: Contrast Sofia's 46 WRCM English probe and 0.6 slope against her 92% Spanish reading accuracy, oral math reasoning strength, WIDA 2.7 level, and 38% missed Tier 2 dosage (8 of 21 sessions).

planningFrame.label: IDEA & EBP rule
planningFrame.guidance: Apply IDEA 34 CFR 300.304 nondiscriminatory assessment mandates, OSEP guidance prohibiting RTI/MTSS delays to parent-requested evaluations, and the exclusionary factor for limited English proficiency.

planningFrame.label: Intervention plan
planningFrame.guidance: Recommend bilingual or native-language reading evaluation, developmental language history interviews, peer-comparison norms, and deconflicted Tier 2 English vocabulary and decoding bridges.

planningFrame.label: Monitoring & safeguards
planningFrame.guidance: Issue Prior Written Notice and obtain informed consent in Spanish, use a qualified bilingual evaluator or trained interpreter, and graph biweekly CBM progress with verified fidelity.

successCriteria: Explicitly rejects delaying the mother's written evaluation request for 12 more weeks of MTSS and cites timely Prior Written Notice and informed parental consent.
Identifies both compromised Tier 2 treatment integrity (8 missed sessions due to ESL pullout) and second-language proficiency as confounds in the English CBM data.
Specifies valid native-language and bilingual assessment procedures under 34 CFR 300.304 rather than relying on English-normed scores alone.
Pairs evaluation compliance with immediate schedule coordination and sheltered English instructional supports so Sofia does not lose reading time.
commonPitfalls: Agreeing with the MTSS lead to postpone IDEA evaluation until Sofia finishes a full 12-week Tier 2 cycle despite a written parent request.
Treating the 46 WRCM English score as direct evidence of dyslexia without comparing Spanish literacy or similarly situated multilingual peers.
Having an untrained bilingual paraprofessional informally translate English standardized test items during the evaluation.
Halting Tier 2 reading and ESL instruction while the 60-day multidisciplinary evaluation timeline is underway.
sampleOutline: Data & fidelity audit: Sofia's 92% Spanish accuracy, WIDA 2.7 profile, and 8 missed Tier 2 sessions show that language transfer barriers and broken dosage confound her 0.6 WRCM/week slope.

Legal timeline compliance: Respond promptly to the mother's written request with Spanish-language Prior Written Notice, procedural safeguards, and consent forms; initiate evaluation without waiting for extra MTSS weeks.

Nondiscriminatory assessment battery: Pair a bilingual speech/school psychologist evaluation with Spanish and English phonics/comprehension measures, caregiver language history, and classroom observations.
Concurrent instructional repair: Realign ESL and Tier 2 schedules to protect full dosage, target explicit English morphological and vocabulary transfer, and track biweekly CBM growth.

constructedResponseWorkshops.title: Align Measurable IEP Goals and SDI Without Diluting Grade-Level Standards
constructedResponseWorkshops.prompt: Revise a flawed draft IEP for a sixth-grade student with a Specific Learning Disability so present levels, measurable annual goals, specially designed instruction, and accommodations preserve grade-level rigor.
constructedResponseWorkshops.stimulus: Marcus (Grade 6, SLD in reading comprehension and writing) decodes multisyllabic science terms at 93% accuracy with text-to-speech, scores 80% on literal questions, and scores 45% on text-dependent inference items. Baseline writing probes average 4 disconnected sentences without evidence. The draft goal states "Marcus will improve reading and writing by 80%" and proposes Grade 3 science worksheets instead of Grade 6 labs with SDI and accommodations.
taskParts: Diagnose the legal and instructional flaws in the draft IEP goal and explain why assigning Grade 3 science worksheets is an unwarranted curriculum modification rather than an accommodation.
Draft a compliant, measurable annual reading-comprehension or written-expression goal linked directly to Marcus's baseline PLAAFP numbers (condition, observable behavior, criterion, timeframe).
Specify evidence-based Specially Designed Instruction (SDI) and classroom/state-assessment accommodations that build independent inference and evidence-based writing in Grade 6 content.

planningFrame.label: Evidence
planningFrame.guidance: Anchor the plan in Marcus's 93% TTS-supported decoding, 80% literal vs. 45% inference comprehension split, and 4-sentence baseline lacking textual citations.

planningFrame.label: IDEA & EBP rule
planningFrame.guidance: Apply IDEA 34 CFR 300.320 IEP content standards, the distinction between construct-preserving accommodations and standard-lowering modifications, and WWC adolescent literacy practices.

planningFrame.label: Intervention plan
planningFrame.guidance: Pair explicit inference and paragraph-structure SDI (modeling, graphic organizers, sentence frames) with Grade 6 science accommodations (TTS, chunked prompts, extended time).

planningFrame.label: Monitoring & safeguards
planningFrame.guidance: Define biweekly curriculum-based comprehension and rubric-scored writing probes, quarterly IEP progress reporting aligned to report cards, and state-assessment accommodation consistency.

successCriteria: Clearly distinguishes accommodations (maintaining Grade 6 cognitive rigor) from modifications (lowering standards to Grade 3 worksheets that narrow graduation pathways).
Writes a measurable annual goal tied directly to Marcus's 45% inference or 4-sentence baseline with explicit condition, skill, mastery criterion, and measurement schedule.
Identifies concrete SDI methods (explicit comprehension strategy modeling, morphological/academic vocabulary work, structured writing routines) distinct from generic classroom accommodations.
Aligns daily classroom accommodations with allowable state assessment supports and establishes objective progress-monitoring routines.
commonPitfalls: Keeping the vague "improve reading and writing by 80%" goal without specifying baseline performance, grade-level text conditions, or measurement tools.
Approving Grade 3 science worksheets to reduce frustration, inadvertently denying Marcus access to the general Grade 6 curriculum.
Listing accommodations like extended time or text-to-speech as though they substitute for Specially Designed Instruction in inference and writing.
Adding accommodations exclusively for state testing that Marcus never practices during daily Grade 6 instruction.
sampleOutline: PLAAFP & goal audit: The draft goal lacks baseline anchors, observable criteria, and measurement procedures, while Grade 3 worksheets improperly modify content standards when Marcus shows 80% literal comprehension.

Measurable goal redesign: Specify that given Grade 6 informational text with text-to-speech and a graphic organizer, Marcus will answer text-dependent inference questions with 80% accuracy across 4 of 5 consecutive biweekly probes within 36 instructional weeks.

SDI vs. accommodations: Deliver explicit small-group SDI in question-answer relationships and claim-evidence-reasoning writing, paired with TTS, chunked lab protocols, and word banks in Grade 6 science.
Progress tracking: Collect biweekly inference probes and analytic writing rubrics, review slope every 6 weeks, and mirror daily accommodations on state assessments.

constructedResponseWorkshops.taskType: LRE placement, UDL access & assistive technology
constructedResponseWorkshops.title: Restore LRE Access Through Assistive Technology and UDL Supplementary Aids
constructedResponseWorkshops.prompt: Review a placement proposal for a fifth-grade student with cerebral palsy and dysarthria to determine how LRE mandates, IDEA assistive technology consideration, and UDL supports govern her instructional setting.
constructedResponseWorkshops.stimulus: Priya (Grade 5, cerebral palsy with dysarthria and fine-motor fatigue) shows grade-level receptive vocabulary and 84% accuracy on Grade 5 fraction problems when responding via her speech-generating AAC tablet. She currently spends 70% of her day in a separate self-contained class solely because the Grade 5 room lacks an adjustable lap tray, switch-accessible math tools, and UDL response options. Her parents request full-day general education.
taskParts: Evaluate the current 70% self-contained placement against IDEA 34 CFR 300.114 LRE requirements and explain why administrative convenience or missing classroom equipment cannot justify removal.
Apply the IDEA 34 CFR 300.324 special-factors mandate for assistive technology and communication to specify the supplementary aids, AAC integration, and UDL math scaffolds Priya needs in Grade 5.
Outline a coordinated general-education transition, staff training, and progress-monitoring plan involving the SLP, OT, general educator, and family.

planningFrame.label: Evidence
planningFrame.guidance: Highlight Priya's grade-level receptive skills and 84% AAC-supported fraction mastery to show her barrier is physical and environmental access rather than cognitive inability.

planningFrame.label: IDEA & EBP rule
planningFrame.guidance: Cite IDEA 34 CFR 300.114 LRE presumption, supplementary aids and services before removal, and 34 CFR 300.324(a)(2) mandatory team consideration of communication and assistive technology.

planningFrame.label: Intervention plan
planningFrame.guidance: Specify UDL multiple means of expression (AAC vocabulary pages for Grade 5 math, digital manipulatives, reduced handwriting load), ergonomic OT positioning, and push-in co-teaching.

planningFrame.label: Monitoring & safeguards
planningFrame.guidance: Document AT devices and staff/family training directly in the IEP, track independent AAC participation and Grade 5 mastery data, and protect full inclusion in nonacademic periods.

successCriteria: Identifies the current 70% separate placement as an LRE violation because removal stems from missing classroom equipment rather than unmet needs despite supplementary aids.
Addresses mandatory IEP consideration of both communication needs and assistive technology devices/services (including staff training and device maintenance) under 34 CFR 300.324.
Embeds concrete UDL representations and expression options (AAC math vocabulary, switch/tablet tools, ergonomic setup) that preserve Priya's active peer participation.
Defines clear collaborative roles for the general educator, special educator, OT, and SLP with objective participation and academic outcome metrics.
commonPitfalls: Recommending that Priya stay in the self-contained classroom until the general educator independently figures out how to program her AAC tablet.
Treating assistive technology solely as hardware delivery while omitting IDEA-covered AT services such as vocabulary customization, troubleshooting, and teacher coaching.
Excusing Priya from collaborative math discourse because AAC responses take slightly longer than spoken replies.
Placing Priya in general education without writing her ergonomic, AAC, and push-in supports explicitly into the IEP supplementary aids section.
sampleOutline: LRE determination: Because Priya achieves 84% on Grade 5 fractions using AAC, keeping her in a separate classroom for 70% of the day based on missing equipment violates 34 CFR 300.114.
AT & UDL design: Document AAC math-vocabulary overlays, switch-accessible digital manipulatives, adjustable OT desk positioning, and extended response wait time under IEP supplementary aids.
Team training & delivery: Schedule SLP and OT consultation to train Grade 5 staff and peers on AAC communication partners and deploy push-in special education support during complex labs.
Access & outcome tracking: Monitor Priya's independent AAC turns per lesson, Grade 5 curriculum mastery, and fatigue levels every 3 weeks with family check-ins.

constructedResponseWorkshops.title: Replace Punitive Hallway Removals with a Function-Matched Math BIP
constructedResponseWorkshops.prompt: Interpret ten days of classroom ABC observations and PBIS context data for a third-grade student with ADHD to design a proactive, function-matched Behavior Intervention Plan.
constructedResponseWorkshops.stimulus: Devon (Grade 3, OHI for ADHD) snaps pencils, calls out, and leaves his seat during 20-minute independent multi-step math blocks. Across 10 ABC observations, 17 of 20 episodes began within 2 minutes of a 15-problem worksheet and ended with a clip-chart move down and 10-minute hallway removal. During partner math fluency games he stays engaged 88% of the time. Tier 1 PBIS expectations are posted on a chart but rarely taught or practiced.
taskParts: Formulate a testable functional hypothesis from the ABC pattern explaining how hallway removals unintentionally reinforce Devon's off-task behavior.
Design a multi-component BIP aligned with PBIS that combines antecedent math scaffolds, explicit teaching of a functionally equivalent replacement behavior, and positive reinforcement.
Establish an implementation fidelity checklist and daily behavioral-academic progress monitoring plan to evaluate whether both work completion and on-task engagement improve.

planningFrame.label: Evidence
planningFrame.guidance: Link the 17 of 20 episodes triggered by 15-problem independent worksheets and terminated by 10-minute hallway removals against Devon's 88% engagement during partner games.

planningFrame.label: IDEA & EBP rule
planningFrame.guidance: Apply functional behavior assessment principles, negative reinforcement (task escape) mechanics, WWC teacher-delivered behavioral intervention guidance, and explicit elementary math scaffolding.

planningFrame.label: Intervention plan
planningFrame.guidance: Replace clip-chart hallway removals with chunked 3-problem math strips, concrete-representational worked examples, a taught break/help signal, and behavior-specific praise.

planningFrame.label: Monitoring & safeguards
planningFrame.guidance: Track daily problems completed accurately, independent use of the help/break card, and off-task frequency alongside weekly adult fidelity checks on antecedent prompts and praise ratios.

successCriteria: Correctly identifies escape from lengthy independent multi-step math tasks (negative reinforcement via hallway removal) as the primary hypothesized function.
Eliminates punitive public clip-chart shaming and hallway removals that both reinforce escape and sever math instruction.
Integrates academic math supports (chunked sets, worked examples, brief partner warm-ups) with explicit replacement-skill teaching (raising a help/check card) and dense reinforcement.
Specifies measurable behavioral and math-completion targets plus adult fidelity monitoring to distinguish plan failure from inconsistent implementation.
commonPitfalls: Mislabeling Devon's calling out as attention-seeking without noting that 85% of episodes end in task escape during independent worksheets.
Increasing punishment severity (longer hallway time or losing recess) instead of teaching an alternative escape/help response and lowering task friction.
Designing a purely behavioral token chart while ignoring the instructional barrier of an unscaffolded 15-problem multi-step worksheet.
Tracking only office referrals rather than daily replacement-skill usage, math accuracy, and staff fidelity.
sampleOutline: Functional hypothesis: When presented with a 15-problem independent multi-step math sheet, Devon snaps pencils and calls out to escape aversive task difficulty, reinforced by 10-minute hallway removals.
Antecedent & Tier 1 PBIS repair: Reteach classroom math-block expectations positively, cut worksheets into 3-problem chunks with a worked model, and open with a 2-minute partner warm-up.

Replacement & consequence plan: Explicitly teach Devon to flip a desk help/check card for 30-second coaching or a brief earned movement reset, paired with a 4-to-1 behavior-specific praise ratio and neutral non-removal redirection.
Progress & fidelity tracking: Graph daily chunk completion, card requests, and off-task counts over 4 weeks alongside twice-weekly fidelity checks on teacher prompting and praise.

constructedResponseWorkshops.title: Enforce Manifestation Determination, PWN, and FAPE Continuity Rules
constructedResponseWorkshops.prompt: Advise a middle school IEP team on mandatory IDEA discipline safeguards after an eighth-grade student with an IEP faces a suspension that exceeds ten cumulative school days.
constructedResponseWorkshops.stimulus: Jordan (Grade 8, IEP for ED and SLD) has already served 8 out-of-school suspension days this semester. Today a substitute gave a surprise quiz without honoring Jordan's IEP quiet break pass or visual preview; Jordan shouted profanity and knocked over a desk. The assistant principal proposes an immediate 5-day suspension (13 cumulative days) and unilateral transfer to an alternative school with no team meeting or written notice.
taskParts: Determine whether the proposed 5-day suspension triggers a disciplinary change of placement under 34 CFR 300.530 and list the mandatory timelines for parent notification, Procedural Safeguards Notice, and Manifestation Determination Review (MDR).
Apply both statutory MDR prongs to Jordan's case—highlighting the direct failure to implement his IEP break pass and visual preview—and state the required legal outcome.
Detail the required FAPE service continuity, FBA/BIP review, and Prior Written Notice safeguards that prevent unilateral placement changes.

planningFrame.label: Evidence
planningFrame.guidance: Note the 8 prior suspension days plus 5 proposed days (13 total, crossing the 10-day threshold) and the substitute's failure to provide Jordan's documented IEP break pass and visual preview.

planningFrame.label: IDEA & EBP rule
planningFrame.guidance: Apply 34 CFR 300.530 (10-day change-of-placement rules, 10-school-day MDR deadline, two-prong manifestation test, return-to-placement mandate) and 34 CFR 300.504 procedural safeguards notice.

planningFrame.label: Intervention plan
planningFrame.guidance: Convene the MDR team within 10 school days, find a manifestation under Prong 2 (and evaluate Prong 1), return Jordan to his placement, conduct/revise his FBA/BIP, and fix substitute IEP handoffs.

planningFrame.label: Monitoring & safeguards
planningFrame.guidance: Provide same-day parent notice and procedural safeguards, guarantee FAPE services beginning on Day 11 of removal, issue PWN for any IEP revision, and block unilateral alternative transfers.

successCriteria: Correctly calculates that 13 cumulative days triggers a change-of-placement review requiring same-day parental notification, Procedural Safeguards Notice, and an MDR within 10 school days.
Applies both MDR prongs accurately, recognizing that failing to provide IEP-mandated supports (break pass and visual preview) establishes a direct manifestation under Prong 2.

States that when conduct is a manifestation (and no weapon, drug, or serious bodily injury special circumstance exists), Jordan must return to his placement unless the parent and LEA agree to a change via the BIP.
Requires immediate remediation of IEP implementation gaps (including substitute folders/training), FBA/BIP revision, and FAPE continuity starting on Day 11.
commonPitfalls: Allowing the assistant principal to transfer Jordan unilaterally to an alternative school without an IEP team decision or parent agreement.
Treating the knocked-over desk as a 45-school-day "special circumstance" removal when no weapon, controlled substance, or serious bodily injury occurred.
Focusing the MDR solely on whether Jordan's disability caused the outburst while overlooking Prong 2 (direct result of the school's failure to implement the IEP).
Omitting FAPE educational services during removals beyond 10 school days or forgetting to send the Procedural Safeguards Notice on the decision date.
sampleOutline: Change-of-placement trigger: Adding 5 days to 8 prior days reaches 13 cumulative days; on the date of the disciplinary decision, notify Jordan's parent and deliver the Procedural Safeguards Notice under 34 CFR 300.504.

Two-prong MDR analysis: Within 10 school days, relevant IEP team members review data; because the substitute omitted IEP-required break and preview supports, Prong 2 (direct result of failure to implement the IEP) is met immediately.
Mandatory remedies: Return Jordan to his agreed placement, immediately correct IEP implementation with substitute-ready accommodation protocols, and conduct or update his FBA and BIP.
FAPE & PWN safeguards: Guarantee educational services starting on the 11th cumulative day of removal and issue Prior Written Notice before any team-agreed IEP or BIP modification.

constructedResponseWorkshops.title: Rebuild Co-Teaching Roles, Fade Para Dependence, and Launch Age-16 Transition
constructedResponseWorkshops.prompt: Restructure collaborative instruction, paraprofessional support, and secondary transition planning for a tenth-grade student whose inclusive program has drifted into prompt dependency and missing transition compliance.
constructedResponseWorkshops.stimulus: Elena (Grade 10, turning 16 next month, Intellectual Disability) attends co-taught biology and English with a 1-to-1 paraprofessional. Walkthroughs show the special educator circulates passively ("one teach, one assist") while the aide writes Elena's lab answers and whispers every step, isolating her from peers. Her draft age-16 IEP lacks transition assessments, measurable postsecondary goals, and any vocational agency planning.
taskParts: Redesign the co-teaching partnership using higher-impact models (such as station, parallel, or alternative teaching) so the special educator delivers authentic SDI rather than serving as a classroom aide.
Establish a paraprofessional supervision and prompt-fading plan that clarifies ethical role boundaries, stops the aide from completing Elena's work, and builds natural peer supports.

Bring Elena's age-16 IEP into compliance with IDEA 34 CFR 300.320(b) secondary transition mandates—including age-appropriate assessments, measurable postsecondary goals, course of study, and student-led participation.

planningFrame.label: Evidence
planningFrame.guidance: Address the three walkthrough gaps together: passive "one teach, one assist" co-teaching, paraprofessional over-prompting/scribing that blocks peer ties, and absent age-16 transition components.

planningFrame.label: IDEA & EBP rule
planningFrame.guidance: Apply IDEA 34 CFR 300.320(b) transition requirements (in effect by age 16, updated annually), LRE natural-support principles under 34 CFR 300.116, and teacher-directed paraprofessional supervision standards.

planningFrame.label: Intervention plan
planningFrame.guidance: Schedule weekly co-planning for station/parallel teaching, implement a least-to-most prompt-fading matrix for the paraprofessional, and administer interest/adaptive transition assessments with Elena.

planningFrame.label: Monitoring & safeguards
planningFrame.guidance: Obtain parental consent before inviting outside vocational rehabilitation agencies, invite Elena to her IEP meeting, and track independent task initiation and peer interaction rates monthly.

successCriteria: Replaces overused "one teach, one assist" routines with structured co-teaching models and shared planning that preserve licensed special-educator delivery of SDI.
Sets explicit paraprofessional boundaries (supporting access rather than completing lab work) paired with a concrete prompt-fading and peer-partnering plan.

Includes all required IDEA age-16 transition elements: age-appropriate transition assessments, measurable postsecondary goals (training/education, employment, and as appropriate independent living), aligned transition services, and course of study.
Notes the legal requirement to invite Elena to her transition IEP meeting and obtain prior written consent from parents (or adult student) before inviting outside agencies.
commonPitfalls: Delegating lesson design, grading, or SDI planning to the paraprofessional rather than providing structured teacher supervision and fading schedules.
Writing generic postsecondary goals ("Elena wants a job") without tying them to age-appropriate transition assessments and measurable annual IEP goals.
Inviting a state vocational rehabilitation counselor to the IEP meeting without first securing written parental consent.
Abruptly removing the paraprofessional overnight without teaching Elena self-monitoring checklists and training natural peer supports first.
sampleOutline: Co-teaching overhaul: Shift from passive "one teach, one assist" to planned station and parallel teaching in biology and English so both teachers share instructional authority and deliver SDI.

Paraprofessional fading: Train the paraprofessional on least-to-most prompting, move seating back during peer lab work, replace scribing with visual checklists/assistive tools, and audit prompt levels biweekly.

Age-16 transition compliance: Administer vocational interest and adaptive skill assessments with Elena and her family, draft measurable postsecondary education/employment/independent-living goals, and align her high school course of study.
Student voice & agency consent: Coach Elena to co-lead part of her IEP meeting and secure written parental consent before inviting vocational rehabilitation representatives.

quickReference.title: Development, IDEA Disability Profiles & Learner Access
quickReference.purpose: Anchors IDEA 13-category eligibility criteria, developmental trajectories, and cross-domain sensory, motor, and health support rules.
checklist: Verify all three IDEA eligibility prongs: qualifying disability category, adverse effect on educational performance, and demonstrated need for specially designed instruction.
Separate cultural, linguistic, or environmental learning differences from intrinsic disability characteristics before attributing delays to an impairment.
Check sensory, motor, fatigue, medication, and health-plan variables that may mask cognitive ability or alter daily classroom access.
formulas: IDEA 13 disability categories (34 CFR 300.8): Autism, Deaf-Blindness, Deafness, Emotional Disturbance, Hearing Impairment, Intellectual Disability, Multiple Disabilities, Orthopedic Impairment, Other Health Impairment (includes ADHD), Specific Learning Disability, Speech or Language Impairment, Traumatic Brain Injury, and Visual Impairment (plus state-option Developmental Delay ages 3 to 9).

IDEA eligibility three-prong gate: (1) meets criteria for a covered disability category, (2) disability adversely affects educational performance (academic and/or functional), and (3) student requires specially designed instruction (SDI); lacking Prong 3 shifts consideration to a Section 504 plan.

Adaptive and medical support plans: Individualized Healthcare Plan (IHP) and Emergency Action Plan (EAP) authored by the school nurse govern chronic medical needs (seizures, asthma, diabetes, feeding), while IDEA mandates school-health nursing services needed to attend school (Cedar Rapids v. Garret F.).

Sensory and executive-function access hierarchy: modify environmental barriers first (lighting, acoustics, positioning, visual schedules, FM/DM systems), then pair explicit skill instruction with assistive technology matched through the SETT framework (Student, Environments, Tasks, Tools).
decisionRules: When a student has a medical diagnosis such as ADHD or asthma with strong academic performance and no need for specially designed instruction → prioritize evaluating for a Section 504 plan and IHP rather than IDEA special education placement.

When an emergent multilingual learner shows reading delays only in English while demonstrating age-appropriate reasoning in the home language → prioritize examining second-language acquisition and instructional history before inferring a disability.

When a student with cerebral palsy or visual impairment misses grade-level responses due to physical or print barriers → prioritize accessible response modes, positioning, and NIMAS/accessible instructional materials before lowering cognitive expectations.

When a student returning from a traumatic brain injury displays sudden fatigue, memory lapses, and emotional lability → prioritize flexible pacing, frequent progress checks, and multidisciplinary re-planning as recovery profiles shift.
cautions: Never assume a clinical or medical diagnosis automatically establishes IDEA eligibility without documented adverse educational impact and a need for specially designed instruction.
Do not rely solely on grade-level academic scores to deny IDEA eligibility; educational performance also encompasses social, communication, behavioral, and functional access.
Avoid altering medical equipment, medication protocols, or health procedures without nurse-delegated training documented in the IHP.

quickReference.domainLabel: Effective Planning and Instruction and Productive Learning Environments
quickReference.title: IEP Architecture, LRE, Explicit Instruction & Behavior
quickReference.purpose: Anchors Endrew F. IEP rigor, LRE placement rules, secondary transition mandates, explicit instruction sequences, and proactive behavior supports.
checklist: Confirm that every annual IEP goal traces directly to objective Present Levels of Academic Achievement and Functional Performance (PLAAFP) baseline data.
Test whether supplementary aids and services can support the student in general education before recommending a more restrictive placement.
Match instructional scaffolds and behavioral supports to observed skill deficits versus performance or environmental barriers.
formulas: Endrew F. v. Douglas County (2017) FAPE standard: an IEP must be reasonably calculated to enable a child to make progress appropriate in light of the child’s circumstances, rejecting the merely more-than-de-minimis floor.

LRE continuum and placement factors (34 CFR 300.114; Rachel H. / Oberti): start in general education with supplementary aids and services, weighing academic benefit, nonacademic benefit, effect on peers/teacher, and placement-after-goals (never predetermine placement by disability label).

IDEA secondary transition mandate (34 CFR 300.320(b)): in effect by the first IEP when the student turns 16 (earlier in some states), requiring age-appropriate transition assessments, measurable postsecondary goals (training/education, employment, independent living), transition services, and transfer-of-rights notice at least 1 year before age of majority.

Explicit instruction and UDL alignment: combine Universal Design for Learning (multiple means of engagement, representation, action/expression) with Explicit Instruction (I Do modeling, We Do guided practice with high opportunities to respond and immediate corrective feedback, You Do independent practice) plus SWPBIS proactive routines (at least 4:1 positive-to-corrective ratio).
decisionRules: When an IEP team discusses moving a student to a self-contained classroom before writing annual goals → prioritize finalizing PLAAFP, measurable goals, and supplementary aids first so placement follows need rather than label.

When a student makes repeated errors during independent seatwork on a newly introduced academic skill → prioritize returning to explicit modeling and high-scaffold guided practice with immediate corrective feedback before assigning independent practice.

When challenging behavior disrupts instruction across predictable classroom transitions → prioritize antecedent prevention (clear expectations, visual schedules, precorrection, active supervision) and teaching a functional replacement behavior.

When a 15-year-old student’s upcoming annual IEP will remain active on their 16th birthday → prioritize conducting age-appropriate transition assessments and inviting the student (and, with parent consent, adult agencies) to draft measurable postsecondary goals.
cautions: Never recycle unchanged IEP goals from year to year when a student fails to make adequate progress; revise instructional intensity, supports, or strategy.
Do not confuse accommodations (change how a student accesses or demonstrates grade-level standards) with modifications (alter the complexity or construct of what is taught or assessed).
Avoid treating LRE as synonymous with full inclusion for every student; IDEA requires maintaining a full continuum of alternative placements based on individual FAPE needs.

quickReference.title: Psychometric Quality, Evaluation Rules & CBM Data Decisions
quickReference.purpose: Anchors IDEA nondiscriminatory evaluation safeguards, technical reliability/validity concepts, accommodation rules, and data-based individualization.
checklist: Verify whether the assessment purpose is screening, diagnostic eligibility, progress monitoring, or summative accountability before selecting an instrument.
Check that assessment tools are administered in the student’s native language or primary mode of communication without cultural or linguistic bias.
Confirm that testing accommodations align with daily classroom accommodations and preserve the target construct being measured.
formulas: IDEA evaluation timelines (34 CFR 300.301 to 300.323): initial evaluation within 60 calendar days of written parental consent (or state-established timeframe), IEP meeting within 30 calendar days of eligibility determination, annual IEP review, and triennial reevaluation at least every 3 years (not more than once per year unless parent and LEA agree).

IDEA nondiscriminatory evaluation rules (34 CFR 300.304): no single measure may determine eligibility; use multiple technically sound instruments across all areas of suspected disability, administered by trained personnel in the child’s native language or mode of communication.

CBM and DBI four-point decision rule: plot weekly curriculum-based measurement scores against an individualized aimline; 4 consecutive data points below the aimline trigger an instructional intensification or adaptation, while 4 consecutive points above the aimline trigger raising the goal.

Assessment type distinctions: norm-referenced tests compare a student to an age/grade peer sample (standard scores, percentiles); criterion-referenced tests measure mastery of defined skills; formative CBM tracks growth over time; accommodations preserve construct validity whereas modifications change target standards.
decisionRules: When 4 consecutive weekly CBM reading fluency scores fall below the student’s aimline despite faithful implementation → prioritize intensifying or adapting the instructional intervention through Data-Based Individualization rather than waiting for the annual IEP review.

When a teacher proposes reading a state reading-comprehension decoding test aloud to a student who has a decoding goal → prioritize checking construct validity and state accommodation policies, because read-aloud may invalidate a decoding construct while remaining valid on a math test.

When a parent submits an outside clinical evaluation disagreeing with school screening findings → prioritize convening the IEP team to consider the external data and obtaining written consent for a comprehensive multidisciplinary evaluation rather than using one test alone.

When a student’s MTSS Tier 2 intervention shows flat growth and the parent requests an IDEA evaluation in writing → prioritize responding promptly with Prior Written Notice and starting the 60-day evaluation timeline without delaying for additional RTI tiers (OSEP Memo 11-07).
cautions: Never use MTSS or RTI tiers to delay or deny an initial IDEA evaluation once a disability is suspected or a parent submits a written evaluation request.
Do not rely on grade-equivalent scores for eligibility or instructional placement decisions because they are ordinal, non-equal-interval values easily misinterpreted by teams.
Avoid testing a student with an unfamiliar accommodation for the first time on a high-stakes state assessment.

quickReference.title: IDEA Safeguards, Discipline MDR, Ethics & Co-Teaching
quickReference.purpose: Anchors IDEA procedural safeguards, 10-day Manifestation Determination Review rules, FERPA privacy, CEC ethics, and collaborative team roles.
checklist: Confirm required written notices, informed parental consent, and native-language translation before proposing or refusing any IEP change.
Count cumulative school-day removals across the school year whenever a student with an IEP faces suspension or disciplinary removal.
Clarify instructional, supervision, and confidentiality boundaries across general educators, related service providers, and paraprofessionals.
formulas: IDEA procedural safeguards (34 CFR 300.500 to 300.518): Prior Written Notice (PWN) before proposing or refusing identification, evaluation, placement, or FAPE; informed written consent for initial evaluation, initial services, and reevaluation; Independent Educational Evaluation (IEE) at public expense if parent disagrees with LEA evaluation; stay-put pendency during disputes; mediation, state complaint (1-year window), and due process (2-year statute).

IDEA discipline and MDR rules (34 CFR 300.530): removals over 10 consecutive school days (or a pattern exceeding 10 cumulative days) constitute a change of placement requiring a Manifestation Determination Review within 10 school days testing two prongs: (1) conduct caused by or directly/substantially related to disability, or (2) direct result of LEA failure to implement the IEP.

MDR outcomes and 45-school-day IAES: if either MDR prong is Yes, return student to placement and conduct FBA/implement or review BIP; exception allows unilateral removal to an Interim Alternative Educational Setting for up to 45 school days only for weapons, illegal drugs, or serious bodily injury (with continued FAPE services).

Co-teaching models (Friend & Cook) and paraprofessional scope: six models (One Teach/One Observe, One Teach/One Assist, Station, Parallel, Alternative, Team Teaching); special educators hold responsibility for planning instruction, writing goals, and communicating with families, while paraprofessionals deliver directed support and collect observational data under supervision.
decisionRules: When an administrator recommends a 5-day suspension for a student with an IEP who already has 7 cumulative days of out-of-school suspension this year → prioritize checking for a disciplinary pattern constituting a change of placement and convening an MDR within 10 school days.

When a parent disagrees with the district’s psychoeducational evaluation and requests an IEE at public expense → prioritize either funding the IEE without unnecessary delay or filing for a due process hearing to defend the district’s evaluation.

When two co-teachers realize one partner consistently acts as an aide in One Teach/One Assist all semester → prioritize shifting to Station, Parallel, or Team Teaching with shared planning to maximize instructional intensity and parity.

When a paraprofessional wants to email a parent directly with a diagnostic opinion or modify an IEP goal independently → prioritize redirecting parent progress conferences and instructional design to the certified special educator while coaching the paraprofessional on FERPA and role boundaries.
cautions: Never conduct an IEP meeting without required members (parent, general educator if participating, special educator, LEA representative, evaluation interpreter) unless formal written excusal rules under 34 CFR 300.321(e) are satisfied.
Do not discuss student IEP details with unauthorized staff or outside providers without documented FERPA parental consent (except legitimate educational interest or health/safety emergency).
Avoid implementing a disciplinary removal exceeding 10 school days without continuing FAPE services needed to progress in the general curriculum and toward IEP goals.

misconceptionFamilies.label: Conflating Accommodations with Curriculum Modifications
misconceptionFamilies.description: Treating changes that alter grade-level academic standards, reduce target concepts, or change grading criteria as accommodations, or withholding legitimate access accommodations such as text-to-speech, extended time, or graphic organizers out of concern that they lower academic rigor.
misconceptionFamilies.remediationMove: Apply the construct-preservation test before choosing a support: if the student demonstrates mastery of the exact same grade-level standard through an adjusted presentation, response, setting, or timing format, it is an accommodation; if the target skill, standard complexity, or mastery criterion changes, it is a modification.

misconceptionFamilies.label: Equating LRE with Automatic Full Inclusion or Category-Based Placement
misconceptionFamilies.description: Assuming Least Restrictive Environment (LRE) requires 100% general education placement regardless of whether the student makes appropriate progress toward FAPE, or assigning a self-contained or resource room based on a disability label or building staffing instead of individual IEP needs.
misconceptionFamilies.remediationMove: Evaluate placement only after IEP goals and supplementary aids and services are defined, starting in general education and moving along the IDEA continuum of alternative placements solely to the extent required for meaningful educational benefit.

misconceptionFamilies.label: Mixing Up IDEA Timelines, Informed Consent Boundaries, and PWN Triggers
misconceptionFamilies.description: Delaying an initial evaluation until tiered RTI cycles finish, treating parent consent to evaluate as consent to begin special education services, misremembering federal 60-day evaluation and 30-day IEP meeting deadlines, or failing to issue Prior Written Notice (PWN) when refusing a parent request.
misconceptionFamilies.remediationMove: Track each IDEA procedural safeguard as a separate legal gate: written informed consent for initial evaluation starts the 60-calendar-day clock (unless state law sets a shorter window), separate written consent is required before initial placement, and PWN is mandatory whenever the district proposes or refuses to initiate or change identification, evaluation, placement, or FAPE.

misconceptionFamilies.label: Applying Routine Discipline Rules Without Manifestation Determination Safeguards
misconceptionFamilies.description: Treating a disciplinary removal exceeding 10 consecutive school days or a pattern of short-term removals over 10 cumulative days as a standard suspension, overlooking the two-prong Manifestation Determination Review (MDR) questions, or misapplying the 45-school-day Interim Alternative Educational Setting (IAES) rule.
misconceptionFamilies.remediationMove: Trigger an MDR within 10 school days of any disciplinary change of placement, test both IDEA prongs (direct/substantial relation to disability and direct result of IEP implementation failure), return the student with an FBA/BIP if either prong is yes, and limit unilateral 45-school-day IAES removals strictly to weapons, drugs, or serious bodily injury.

misconceptionFamilies.label: Misusing Norm-Referenced Tests for Progress Monitoring or Ignoring Cultural and Linguistic Bias
misconceptionFamilies.description: Using broad norm-referenced achievement batteries to guide weekly instructional adjustments instead of curriculum-based measurement (CBM), relying on a single test score for IDEA eligibility, or interpreting normal second-language acquisition and cultural communication patterns as a disability.
misconceptionFamilies.remediationMove: Match every instrument to its psychometric purpose (norm-referenced for peer comparison, criterion-referenced for standard mastery, CBM for frequent progress monitoring), require multiple nondiscriminatory measures administered in the student's native language or most accurate communication mode, and rule out limited English proficiency before eligibility.

misconceptionFamilies.label: Writing Unmeasurable IEP Goals Disconnected from PLAAFP and Misusing Co-Teaching or Paraprofessionals
misconceptionFamilies.description: Drafting broad, label-driven IEP goals without baseline PLAAFP impact data or observable mastery criteria, treating co-teaching as permanent One Teach, One Assist, or delegating initial lesson design and primary instructional decision-making to a paraprofessional.
misconceptionFamilies.remediationMove: Anchor every annual IEP goal directly to an observable PLAAFP deficit using condition, measurable behavior, and mastery criterion; select co-teaching models (Station, Parallel, Alternative, Team Teaching) to maximize active instruction; and restrict paraprofessionals to teacher-planned, supervised support.

misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.title: Apply the Construct-Preservation Test to Separate Accommodations from Modifications
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.recognitionCue: A 5355 scenario describes a classroom or testing support—such as audio read-aloud, reducing ten problems to five covering fewer skills, or grading only content ideas—and asks whether it preserves grade-level standards or alters the assessed construct.
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.repairQuestion: After this support is applied, is the student still being held to the exact same grade-level academic construct and mastery standard, or has the learning expectation itself been reduced or substituted?

stages.label: Recognize
stages.instruction: Identify the target construct being taught or tested in the vignette (for example, reading decoding versus science concept comprehension) and inspect whether the proposed support changes access or changes the standard.
stages.requiredOutput: Label the target academic construct and flag any distractor that either mislabels a standard reduction as an accommodation or restricts an access tool that leaves the construct intact.

stages.label: Repair
stages.instruction: Sort supports along the four accommodation categories (presentation, response, setting, timing/scheduling) versus curriculum modifications (altered content depth, simplified learning goals, reduced standard coverage, modified grading scale) and verify alignment with state assessment rules.
stages.requiredOutput: Write a two-column rule contrasting when text-to-speech is a valid accommodation (math or science assessment) versus when it alters the measured construct (oral decoding fluency assessment).

stages.label: Targeted practice
stages.instruction: Classify four IEP supports for a sixth-grade student with dyslexia: (a) providing audiobooks for a social studies unit, (b) reducing a 20-word spelling list to 8 simpler second-grade words, (c) dictating a history essay via speech-to-text, and (d) replacing a multi-step fraction test with single-digit addition.
stages.requiredOutput: Assign each support to Accommodation or Modification and explain in one sentence per item how the grade-level standard is preserved or altered.

stages.label: Retry & transfer
stages.instruction: Re-read a 5355 IEP-team item where a general education teacher asks whether letting a student use a multiplication chart or shortened assignment compromises fairness, then pick the legally and instructionally sound recommendation.
stages.requiredOutput: Select the response that matches IEP-documented accommodations to daily instruction and testing without unilaterally modifying standards or creating an accommodation-only test surprise.

misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.familyLabel: Equating LRE with Automatic Full Inclusion or Category-Based Placement
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.title: Sequence IEP Goals, Supplementary Aids, and the IDEA LRE Continuum Before Placement
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.recognitionCue: A placement vignette tempts you either to keep a student in general education with zero documented progress just to maximize inclusion, or to jump straight to a self-contained classroom because of a disability label or district program structure.
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.repairQuestion: Has the IEP team first written individualized goals and tested supplementary aids and services in general education before considering a more restrictive setting along the IDEA continuum to guarantee FAPE?

stages.label: Recognize
stages.instruction: Check the stem for two legal traps: predetermination by disability category or administrative convenience, and treating LRE as a single fixed location rather than a continuum anchored to FAPE progress (Endrew F. standard).
stages.requiredOutput: Identify whether the distractor commits category-based predetermination or ignores FAPE benefit in the current environment.

stages.label: Repair
stages.instruction: Order the statutory IEP decision sequence (PLAAFP → measurable annual goals → services and supplementary aids → LRE placement determination) and map the IDEA continuum from general education with supports to resource, separate class, separate school, residential, and home/hospital.
stages.requiredOutput: State why placement is always the final IEP decision and list three supplementary aids and services that must be considered before removing a student from general education.

stages.label: Targeted practice
stages.instruction: Evaluate two scenarios: (1) a principal says all newly identified fourth graders with autism attend the district's self-contained cluster site, and (2) an IEP team sees a student failing to progress in general education reading even with co-teaching and AT and considers targeted pull-out decoding instruction.
stages.requiredOutput: Explain why scenario 1 violates IDEA LRE predetermination rules and how scenario 2 properly uses the continuum while preserving general education participation in non-reading periods.

stages.label: Retry & transfer
stages.instruction: Solve a fresh 5355 placement item asking what the IEP team must document when proposing part-time resource services for a student with significant academic needs.
stages.requiredOutput: Choose the option that documents why satisfactory education cannot be achieved in general education even with supplementary aids and services, plus the exact extent of nonparticipation.

misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.familyLabel: Mixing Up IDEA Timelines, Informed Consent Boundaries, and PWN Triggers
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.title: Lock In IDEA Statutory Clocks, Dual Consent Gates, and Prior Written Notice Rules
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.recognitionCue: An item mentions a parent submitting a written evaluation request, revoking consent, requesting a new service the school declines, or waiting for RTI cycles to conclude before testing.
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.repairQuestion: Which exact IDEA procedural safeguard is triggered right now—evaluation consent, placement consent, Prior Written Notice (PWN), or a federal statutory timeline—and what action is legally prohibited?

stages.label: Recognize
stages.instruction: Spot the exact procedural trigger in the prompt (initial referral, parent refusal/revocation of consent, proposed or refused IEP change, triennial re-evaluation) and flag any distractor that stalls evaluation for RTI or skips written notice.
stages.requiredOutput: Name the triggered IDEA safeguard and identify the procedural violation embedded in the tempting distractor.

stages.label: Repair
stages.instruction: Map the core federal IDEA clocks and consent rules: 60 calendar days from written consent to initial evaluation completion (unless state law is shorter), 30 calendar days from eligibility to initial IEP meeting, annual IEP review, 3-year re-evaluation, separate written consent for evaluation versus initial services, and parent right to revoke consent in writing (ending services after PWN, with no due-process override for initial services).
stages.requiredOutput: Create a 4-line procedural reference table pairing each event (parent referral, district refusal, initial placement, parent revocation) with the required notice, consent rule, and deadline.

stages.label: Targeted practice
stages.instruction: Determine the legally compliant response to three cases: (a) a parent requests an evaluation in writing while the child is in week 3 of Tier 2 RTI, (b) a parent signs evaluation consent so the school starts pull-out services immediately after testing, and (c) the team declines a parent's request for an assistive device.
stages.requiredOutput: Specify the exact IDEA-compliant step for each case, explicitly noting where PWN or separate written consent is required.

stages.label: Retry & transfer
stages.instruction: Re-read a 5355 procedural-safeguards vignette involving either an Independent Educational Evaluation (IEE) at public expense or parent revocation of special education services.
stages.requiredOutput: Select the option that follows IDEA's exact legal duty (either fund the IEE or file due process without unnecessary delay; honor written revocation with PWN and cease services).

misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.familyLabel: Applying Routine Discipline Rules Without Manifestation Determination Safeguards
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.title: Execute the IDEA 10-Day Change-of-Placement, MDR Two-Prong, and IAES Decision Tree
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.recognitionCue: A student with an IEP accumulates repeated short-term suspensions or faces a long-term suspension/expulsion, and distractors either treat the removal like any nondisabled student or skip the FBA/BIP return-to-placement requirement.
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.repairQuestion: Does this removal exceed 10 consecutive school days or create a pattern over 10 cumulative days, and what must follow from each outcome of the two-prong Manifestation Determination Review (MDR)?

stages.label: Recognize
stages.instruction: Count consecutive and cumulative suspension days in the vignette and check whether the incident involves one of IDEA's three 45-school-day special circumstances (weapons, illegal drugs/controlled substances, or serious bodily injury at school or a school function).
stages.requiredOutput: State whether a disciplinary change of placement has occurred and whether the 45-school-day IAES exception applies.

stages.label: Repair
stages.instruction: Apply the two MDR prongs within 10 school days: (1) was the conduct caused by or directly and substantially related to the disability, or (2) was it the direct result of the LEA's failure to implement the IEP? Contrast the mandatory next steps for a "yes" finding (immediate return to placement unless special circumstances or parent agrees, plus FBA and BIP creation/review) versus a "no" finding (same discipline as peers, but FAPE services continue starting day 11).
stages.requiredOutput: Outline the branching outcomes for MDR-Yes, MDR-No, and 45-school-day IAES, including continuation of FAPE services.

stages.label: Targeted practice
stages.instruction: Walk through two discipline cases: (a) a student with ADHD and EBD hits 12 cumulative suspension days across similar classroom-escape incidents and the team learns the BIP was never shared with the substitute teacher, and (b) a student with SLD brings a weapon to campus.
stages.requiredOutput: Determine the MDR ruling for case (a) via prong 2 and specify the exact placement, FBA/BIP, and FAPE actions for both case (a) and case (b).

stages.label: Retry & transfer
stages.instruction: Evaluate a new 5355 legal scenario where an administrator wants to suspend a student with an IEP for 15 days without educational services because the offense violated the zero-tolerance code of conduct.
stages.requiredOutput: Choose the legally required IEP-team action (convene MDR within 10 school days and maintain FAPE services beyond day 10) and reject zero-tolerance exclusion distractors.

misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.familyLabel: Misusing Norm-Referenced Tests for Progress Monitoring or Ignoring Cultural and Linguistic Bias
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.title: Match Assessment Purpose and Nondiscriminatory Safeguards to IDEA Decisions
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.recognitionCue: An assessment item asks how to monitor biweekly IEP reading growth or evaluate a multilingual student, and distractors offer a standardized norm-referenced battery, a single IQ score, or English-only testing.
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.repairQuestion: Does the decision require peer comparison, standard mastery, or frequent growth sensitivity—and how does the evaluation prevent cultural, linguistic, or sensory bias from masquerading as disability?

stages.label: Recognize
stages.instruction: Identify the decision context (universal screening, eligibility evaluation, diagnostic skill pinpointing, or ongoing IEP progress monitoring) and inspect the student's home language, cultural background, and sensory/motor access needs.
stages.requiredOutput: State the exact assessment decision and flag any distractor that uses an insensitive norm-referenced score for weekly tracking or tests an emergent bilingual solely in English.

stages.label: Repair
stages.instruction: Differentiate norm-referenced tests (rank against peer sample; low instructional sensitivity), criterion-referenced tests (measure mastery of defined objectives), and CBM/CBA (brief, repeated probes sensitive to weekly growth), alongside IDEA nondiscriminatory evaluation rules (multiple measures, native language/mode unless clearly not feasible, trained interpreters, no single procedure as sole criterion).
stages.requiredOutput: Map each assessment type to its valid use and list three safeguards required before determining eligibility for a culturally and linguistically diverse student.

stages.label: Targeted practice
stages.instruction: Select the right assessment plan for two students: (1) a fifth grader with an IEP reading-fluency goal whose teacher needs data every two weeks, and (2) a newly arrived Spanish-speaking third grader scoring low on an English vocabulary subtest.
stages.requiredOutput: Recommend CBM oral-reading-fluency probes with aimline graphing for student 1, and bilingual/native-language evaluation plus language-dominance and opportunity-to-learn review for student 2.

stages.label: Retry & transfer
stages.instruction: Re-read a 5355 assessment vignette testing reliability, validity, standard error of measurement (SEM), or disproportionate representation.
stages.requiredOutput: Select the response that interprets scores using confidence bands and multiple converging data sources rather than a single raw score or grade equivalent.

misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.familyLabel: Writing Unmeasurable IEP Goals Disconnected from PLAAFP and Misusing Co-Teaching or Paraprofessionals
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.title: Align PLAAFP Baselines, Measurable IEP Goals, Co-Teaching Models, and Paraprofessional Scope
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.recognitionCue: A planning or collaboration item offers an IEP goal with vague verbs ("understand," "improve"), defaults co-teachers to One Teach, One Assist every day, or lets a paraprofessional create and grade independent lessons.
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.repairQuestion: Does every IEP goal trace directly to a quantified PLAAFP need with observable mastery criteria, and are licensed teachers—not paraprofessionals—owning instructional design across active co-teaching structures?

stages.label: Recognize
stages.instruction: Audit the draft IEP goal for missing PLAAFP linkage, non-observable verbs, or missing mastery/timeframe criteria, and audit team roles for passive co-teaching or unauthorized paraprofessional delegation.
stages.requiredOutput: Pinpoint the exact missing IEP-goal element or collaboration role boundary violation in the stem.

stages.label: Repair
stages.instruction: Apply the four-part measurable goal formula (Condition + Observable Behavior + Mastery Criterion + Timeframe/Measurement Method) anchored to PLAAFP baseline data, match co-teaching models to instructional purpose (Parallel/Station for lower student-teacher ratio, Alternative for targeted preteaching/remediation, Team for dual modeling), and clarify paraprofessional duties (reinforcing teacher-planned instruction and collecting data under direct supervision).
stages.requiredOutput: Rewrite a vague goal ("Student will improve paragraph writing") into a complete measurable annual goal and pair two co-teaching models with their best classroom use cases.

stages.label: Targeted practice
stages.instruction: Fix two collaboration breakdowns: (a) a special educator stands at the back of an inclusive algebra class circulating silently all semester, and (b) a general educator asks a paraprofessional to introduce a brand-new reading comprehension unit and modify the test for three IEP students.
stages.requiredOutput: Propose an active co-teaching shift (such as Station or Alternative Teaching with shared planning) for (a) and reassign initial instruction and test modification to the licensed teachers while specifying the paraprofessional's supervised reinforcement role in (b).

stages.label: Retry & transfer
stages.instruction: Evaluate a fresh 5355 item asking which IEP component or collaborative practice best ensures alignment between student needs and classroom delivery.
stages.requiredOutput: Choose the option that links quantitative PLAAFP data to measurable goals, active co-teaching parity, and legally compliant paraprofessional supervision.
